baseline.gap: Object/heap/image accounts shared a principal ceiling, but each root/thread obtained fresh private-table/stack allowance. Initial x86 root backing preceded authority binding.

policy.new_dimensions: Initial/private table pages and full configured user + 16 kernel data pages for every user-thread stack, alongside existing object/heap/image backing.

implementation.constructor: After signature/metadata/layout validation, prepare the existing admitted boot-lifetime principal record and typed sponsor before architecture root construction. x86 binds before its first PML4 reservation; AArch64 before lazy allocation. Keep original trusted classification. Failure/abandonment cannot shed this captured charge.
implementation.binding: Authority installation validates prebound table principal/amount, excludes already charged tables from aggregate admission, and attaches remaining owners only after one successful reservation. Raw trusted fixture roots can still admit prior tables; no signed-loader unbound fallback.
implementation.tables: Existing private Account holds typed aggregate share behind ManuallyDrop. Reserve before physical work, keep cached prefixes and quarantined provisional pages, refund only confirmed unused/physical release. Incomplete physical walks retain original totals. Shared kernel tables retain their independent policy.
implementation.stacks: Borrow captured sponsor with root lease/table validation, reserve configured maximum user + kernel capacity before allocation, and store typed share in the existing stack Reservation. Pool rejection drops unused share after pool guard exit. Explicit complete/unused refund consumes once; inert field Drop retains on rejection/abandonment. Growth pays no second data charge. New table branches pay separately.
implementation.pure_kernel_threads: No application principal is invented; retain existing trusted kernel-only stack/node policy.
remaining: general kernel heap/metadata and principal-record storage
shared kernel tables, IOMMU/device, capability/IPC/completion and other aggregate families
pure kernel/inherited work without application sponsorship
principal-record lookup/IRQ hold times, concurrent EL0 pressure and restart churn
protected management/timer/teardown progress and per-principal fair shares on small nodes
historical publication lookup, reclamation timeout, restoration-check failures and lost response remain unresolved in their original causal scope
